title: Effect of Palrnatine on lipopolysaccharide-induced acute lung injury by inhibiting activation of the Akt/NF‍-kappaB pathway.
authors: Kan, Xingchi; Chen, Yingsheng; Huang, Bingxu; Fu, Shoupeng; Guo, Wenjin; Ran, Xin; Cao, Yu; Xu, Dianwen; Cheng, Ji; Yang, Zhanqing; Xu, Yanling
journal: Journal of Zhejiang University. Science. B
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然产物Palrnatine通过抑制Akt/NF-kappaB通路缓解急性肺损伤，虽含分子动力学模拟，但核心是药物-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题无关。
abstract: Inflammation plays an important role in the development of acute lung injury (ALI). Severe pulmonary inflammation can cause acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) or even death. Expression of proinflammatory interleukin-‍1beta (IL-‍1beta) and inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) in the process of pulmonary inflammation will further exacerbate the severity of ALI. The purpose of this study was to explore the effect of Palrnatine (Pa) on lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced mouse ALI and its underlying mechanism. Pa, a natural product, has a wide range of pharmacological activities with the potential to protect against lung injury. Western blotting and quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) assays were performed to detect the expression and translation of inflammatory genes and proteins in vitro and in vivo. Immunoprecipitation was used to detect the degree of P65 translocation into the nucleus. We also used molecular modeling to further clarify the mechanism of action. The results showed that Pa pretreatment could significantly inhibit the expression and secretion of the inflammatory cytokine IL-1beta, and significantly reduce the protein level of the proinflammatory protease iNOS, in both in vivo and in vitro models induced by LPS. Further mechanism studies showed that Pa could significantly inhibit the activation of the protein kinase B (Akt)/nuclear factor-kappaB (NF-kappaB) signaling pathway in the LPS-induced ALI mode and in LPS-induced RAW264.7 cells. Through molecular dynamics simulation, we observed that Pa was bound to the catalytic pocket of Akt and effectively inhibited the biological activity of Akt. These results indicated that Pa significantly relieves LPS-induced ALI by activating the Akt/NF-kappaB signaling pathway.
abstract_zh: 炎症在急性肺损伤（ALI）的发生发展中起着重要作用。严重的肺部炎症可导致急性呼吸窘迫综合征（ARDS）甚至死亡。在肺部炎症过程中，促炎性白细胞介素-1β（IL-1β）和诱导型一氧化氮合酶（iNOS）的表达将进一步加剧ALI的严重程度。本研究旨在探讨帕尔马汀（Pa）对脂多糖（LPS）诱导的小鼠ALI的影响及其潜在机制。Pa作为一种天然产物，具有广泛的药理活性，具有保护肺损伤的潜力。采用蛋白质印迹法和实时定量聚合酶链反应（qRT-PCR）检测体外和体内炎症基因和蛋白质的表达及翻译情况。免疫沉淀法用于检测P65向细胞核转位的程度。我们还使用分子建模进一步阐明其作用机制。结果表明，在LPS诱导的体内和体外模型中，Pa预处理能显著抑制炎症细胞因子IL-1β的表达和分泌，并显著降低促炎蛋白酶iNOS的蛋白水平。进一步的机制研究表明，Pa能显著抑制LPS诱导的ALI模型及LPS诱导的RAW264.7细胞中蛋白激酶B（Akt）/核因子-κB（NF-κB）信号通路的激活。通过分子动力学模拟，我们观察到Pa与Akt的催化口袋结合，并有效抑制Akt的生物学活性。这些结果表明，Pa通过激活Akt/NF-κB信号通路显著缓解LPS诱导的ALI。
